quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: Maya quit her job ____ she'd been offered a much better position at a rival company.
quests.sentence: Maya quit her job ____ she'd been offered a much better position at a rival company.
quests.hint: This is fresh, new information explaining her decision, not something already known or a formal literary reflection.
quests.explanation: 'Because' fits this direct, everyday explanation of new information. 'Since' would suggest this reason was already an established fact going into the sentence, and 'for' would sound oddly literary for this casual context.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the client had already signed off on the budget, the team proceeded without further review.
quests.sentence: ____ the client had already signed off on the budget, the team proceeded without further review.
quests.hint: This clause presents an already-settled fact as the basis for what follows - notice it opens the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Since' introduces this established, already-known fact as the reason for proceeding. 'Because' would also give a reason but doesn't carry quite the same 'given that this is already true' framing.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The captain refused to abandon ship, ____ he had given his word to see the crew home safely.
quests.sentence: The captain refused to abandon ship, ____ he had given his word to see the crew home safely.
quests.hint: This reads like a formal, literary reflection - the reason follows a comma in that reflective narrative style.
quests.explanation: 'For' fits this formal, literary register well. 'Because' would also give a reason but sounds more conversational than this reflective narration.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The librarian moved the reference desk closer to the entrance ____ new visitors could find help right away.
quests.sentence: The librarian moved the reference desk closer to the entrance ____ new visitors could find help right away.
quests.hint: This relocation was a deliberate choice made with a specific goal in mind - helping new visitors.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'could' expressing the enabled benefit. 'So' alone would instead suggest this was an unplanned side effect rather than a deliberate decision.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The reference desk was moved closer to the entrance, ____ visitors now find help within seconds of walking in.
quests.sentence: The reference desk was moved closer to the entrance, ____ visitors now find help within seconds of walking in.
quests.hint: This describes the actual, current outcome of the move, not a stated goal with a modal verb like 'could.'
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces this straightforward, factual result. 'So that' would need a modal verb to properly express a purpose, which isn't how this sentence is phrased.
quests.grammarRule: Result vs Purpose - so, not so that

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The airline lowered the minimum connection time by ten minutes ____ tighter layovers could still work for most travelers.
quests.sentence: The airline lowered the minimum connection time by ten minutes ____ tighter layovers could still work for most travelers.
quests.hint: This policy change was made with a specific goal in mind - making tighter layovers workable.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'could' expressing the enabled outcome. 'So' alone would instead suggest this was an unplanned effect.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: Some people on the team prefer working from the office every day, ____ others are much happier with a fully remote setup.
quests.sentence: Some people on the team prefer working from the office every day, ____ others are much happier with a fully remote setup.
quests.hint: This casual comparison between coworker preferences doesn't need the more formal, report-like connector.
quests.explanation: 'While' compares these two contrasting preferences in a natural, everyday way. 'Whereas' would also work but sounds a touch more formal than this casual observation calls for.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the pilot study used a small sample of twenty participants, the follow-up research surveyed over a thousand.
quests.sentence: ____ the pilot study used a small sample of twenty participants, the follow-up research surveyed over a thousand.
quests.hint: This is formal academic language comparing two study designs - the more formal comparison connector fits here.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' suits this formal, academic register well. 'While' would also technically work but feels less suited to this precise, report-like comparison.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The new employee had almost no experience in the industry, ____ she outperformed every veteran on the team within her first month.
quests.sentence: The new employee had almost no experience in the industry, ____ she outperformed every veteran on the team within her first month.
quests.hint: Outperforming veterans despite having no experience is a genuine surprise, not simply two facts being compared side by side.
quests.explanation: 'But' captures this unexpected, impressive turnaround. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising twist.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the forecast stays clear, the outdoor wedding will go ahead as planned.
quests.sentence: ____ the forecast stays clear, the outdoor wedding will go ahead as planned.
quests.hint: This is a simple, straightforward condition - no 'regardless' sense and no built-in negative.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces this plain, positive condition. 'Unless' would reverse the meaning, and 'even if' would add an unnecessary sense of 'no matter what' that isn't needed here.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The outdoor wedding will be moved indoors ____ the forecast stays clear through Saturday.
quests.sentence: The outdoor wedding will be moved indoors ____ the forecast stays clear through Saturday.
quests.hint: Moving indoors happens specifically when clear weather does NOT hold through Saturday - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the move indoors depends on the forecast failing to stay clear. 'If' would need 'doesn't stay' added to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The couple has decided to hold the ceremony outdoors ____ the forecast turns unfavorable at the last minute.
quests.sentence: The couple has decided to hold the ceremony outdoors ____ the forecast turns unfavorable at the last minute.
quests.hint: Their decision holds firm no matter what happens with the weather - stronger than a simple condition.
quests.explanation: 'Even if' shows their plan stays the same regardless of a possible weather change. 'Unless' would incorrectly suggest bad weather could actually change their decision.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The factory temporarily halted production ____ a critical safety inspection had flagged several violations.
quests.sentence: The factory temporarily halted production ____ a critical safety inspection had flagged several violations.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason for halting production, which already happened.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the halt. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the halt the cause of the flagged violations.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ ticket prices had increased significantly this season, attendance at home games stayed just as high as last year.
quests.sentence: ____ ticket prices had increased significantly this season, attendance at home games stayed just as high as last year.
quests.hint: Attendance staying high despite higher prices is the unexpected twist here, not simply two facts being compared.
quests.explanation: 'Although' captures this concession between the price increase and the steady attendance. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts side by side.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the last box was finally unpacked, the apartment finally started to feel like home.
quests.sentence: ____ the last box was finally unpacked, the apartment finally started to feel like home.
quests.hint: Unpacking the last box is the specific trigger for the feeling to change, not something ongoing up to that point.
quests.explanation: 'Once' captures the idea that finishing the unpacking directly triggered this feeling. 'Until' would incorrectly suggest something continued up to that point rather than starting right after it.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: Submit your expense report ____ the end of the month to avoid processing delays.
quests.sentence: Submit your expense report ____ the end of the month to avoid processing delays.
quests.hint: This is about a single deadline to beat, not an ongoing stretch of time or a trigger for something else.
quests.explanation: 'Before' marks the submission deadline as a single point to meet. 'Until' would incorrectly suggest an ongoing action continuing up to that point, rather than a one-time deadline.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The negotiations dragged on ____ both sides finally reached a compromise after midnight.
quests.sentence: The negotiations dragged on ____ both sides finally reached a compromise after midnight.
quests.hint: The negotiations continued without stopping, right up to the moment of the compromise - this is about ongoing duration.
quests.explanation: 'Until' captures this continuous dragging-on that stops exactly at the compromise. 'Before' would only mark a single point, missing the sense of prolonged, ongoing negotiation.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The museum stays open late on Thursdays ____ nine in the evening.
quests.sentence: The museum stays open late on Thursdays ____ nine in the evening.
quests.hint: This marks the closing boundary of an extended opening period, not a single deadline to meet beforehand.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the extended hours run continuously up to nine. 'Before' would instead suggest something needs to happen prior to nine, which isn't the meaning here.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the final payment clears, ownership of the property officially transfers to the buyers.
quests.sentence: ____ the final payment clears, ownership of the property officially transfers to the buyers.
quests.hint: The payment clearing is the specific, deliberate trigger for the legal transfer, not just a general point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Once' emphasizes that the cleared payment directly triggers the ownership transfer. 'When' could describe simple timing but doesn't capture this completion-triggers-next-step relationship as precisely.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The fireworks display begins ____ the sun has fully set over the harbor.
quests.sentence: The fireworks display begins ____ the sun has fully set over the harbor.
quests.hint: This is simply the next event in a straightforward sequence, without a special sense of 'triggered by completion.'
quests.explanation: 'After' shows the fireworks follow the sunset in simple sequence. 'Once' would also work but adds an unnecessary emphasis on the sunset being a deliberate trigger, which isn't needed for this natural, expected sequence.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the microwave beeps three times, the popcorn is usually ready.
quests.sentence: ____ the microwave beeps three times, the popcorn is usually ready.
quests.hint: This is a simple, routine point in time - no special emphasis on triggering or completing something is needed here.
quests.explanation: 'When' fits this simple, routine timing well. 'Once' would add an unnecessary sense of deliberate triggering that this everyday observation doesn't need.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ visitors wouldn't have to wait in long lines, the theme park added six new ticket booths this summer.
quests.sentence: ____ visitors wouldn't have to wait in long lines, the theme park added six new ticket booths this summer.
quests.hint: This was a deliberate improvement made with a specific goal in mind - shorter wait times.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'wouldn't' expressing the intended benefit. 'Because' would incorrectly frame shorter waits as an existing reason rather than a goal.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the recipe had never failed her in fifteen years of baking, Grace decided to test it twice before the wedding.
quests.sentence: ____ the recipe had never failed her in fifteen years of baking, Grace decided to test it twice before the wedding.
quests.hint: Fifteen years without a single failure is a strong track record - this deserves the stronger of the two near-identical concession connectors.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes the strength of her reliable track record, making her extra caution feel notably careful. 'Although' would also technically work, but doesn't carry quite the same weight given how long and consistent her success had been.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The east coast office handles all client onboarding, ____ the west coast office focuses exclusively on technical support.
quests.sentence: The east coast office handles all client onboarding, ____ the west coast office focuses exclusively on technical support.
quests.hint: Two different offices with two different roles are simply being compared here.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting office roles. 'Although' would suggest one office focuses on support despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: You can borrow my car this weekend ____ you fill up the tank before you bring it back.
quests.sentence: You can borrow my car this weekend ____ you fill up the tank before you bring it back.
quests.hint: This sets a clear, ongoing requirement in a fairly casual, personal favor, not a formal contract.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' fits this everyday requirement well. 'Provided that' would sound oddly formal for a casual favor between friends, and 'if' would also work but doesn't carry quite the same firm, rule-like feel.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the vendor delivers the materials by Friday, the construction timeline will not be affected.
quests.sentence: ____ the vendor delivers the materials by Friday, the construction timeline will not be affected.
quests.hint: This reads like formal project or contract language - the most formal of the near-identical condition phrases fits best.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' matches this formal, official tone. 'If' and 'as long as' would also technically work but feel less suited to this precise, contract-like register.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ you're around this weekend, we should grab coffee.
quests.sentence: ____ you're around this weekend, we should grab coffee.
quests.hint: This is a casual, simple invitation - the plain, everyday condition word fits naturally here.
quests.explanation: 'If' fits this casual, simple question naturally. 'Provided that' or 'as long as' would sound oddly formal or demanding for such a relaxed invitation.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The quarterly report was released a week early ____ several board members had requested the numbers ahead of the annual meeting.
quests.sentence: The quarterly report was released a week early ____ several board members had requested the numbers ahead of the annual meeting.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason the report came out early, not an outcome, contrast, or condition.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the early release. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the early release the cause of the board's request.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the two candidates had nearly identical qualifications on paper, the hiring committee felt strongly that one was the clearly better fit.
quests.sentence: ____ the two candidates had nearly identical qualifications on paper, the hiring committee felt strongly that one was the clearly better fit.
quests.hint: The committee's strong preference despite nearly identical qualifications is the unexpected twist - not simply two resumes being compared.
quests.explanation: 'Although' captures this concession between the similar qualifications and the committee's strong, decisive preference. 'Whereas' would only fit for a neutral comparison, missing this sense of an unexpected, strong reaction.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the project lead grants individual editing permissions, the shared document will remain view-only for the whole team.
quests.sentence: ____ the project lead grants individual editing permissions, the shared document will remain view-only for the whole team.
quests.hint: Staying view-only happens specifically when permissions are NOT granted - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the document stays locked specifically without granted permissions. 'Until' would instead suggest the restriction is just temporary and time-based, rather than genuinely dependent on this action being taken.
